title: Sales-personnel training, self-certification and its fee, and employment measures for regulated sellers of scheduled listed chemical products
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1314.35 and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(A)(vii)-(viii), each regulated seller must ensure that, for individuals who are responsible for delivering scheduled listed chemical products into the custody of purchasers or who deal directly with purchasers by obtaining payments for the products, the seller has submitted to the Administration a self-certification that all such individuals have, in accordance with criteria issued by the Administration, undergone training provided by the seller to ensure that they understand the requirements of part 1314, and that the seller maintains a copy of each self-certification and all records demonstrating that those individuals have undergone the training. Under 21 CFR 1314.40 and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(B), a regulated seller must submit that self-certification in order to sell any scheduled listed chemical product; the certification is not effective unless it also includes a statement that the seller understands each of the requirements of the part and agrees to comply with them; when the seller files the initial self-certification the Administration assigns it to one of twelve groups, the self-certifications of a group expire on the last day of the month designated for that group, and the Administration may select a group with an expiration date that is not less than 12 months or more than 23 months from the date of the self-certification; after the initial certification period the seller must update the self-certification annually; and the seller must provide a separate certification for each place of business at which it sells scheduled listed chemical products at retail. Under 21 CFR 1314.42 the seller must pay a fee of $21 for each initial application to self-certify and for the renewal of each existing self-certification, at the time of self-certification, by credit card, and the fee is not refundable, but the fee is waived for any person holding a current DEA registration in good standing as a pharmacy to dispense controlled substances. Under 21 CFR 1314.50 and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(G), a regulated seller may take reasonable measures to guard against employing individuals who may present a risk with respect to the theft and diversion of scheduled listed chemical products, which may include, notwithstanding State law, asking applicants for employment whether they have been convicted of any crime involving or related to such products or controlled substances.
exam_relevance: Tests the store-level prerequisites to any sale: whom the seller must train, that self-certification precedes selling and must carry the statement of understanding and agreement, that each place of business certifies separately and updates annually, and that the $21 fee is waived for a DEA-registered pharmacy while the certification itself is not.

exceptions: 21 CFR 1314.42(b) waives the self-certification fee for any person holding a current DEA registration in good standing as a pharmacy to dispense controlled substances; it waives only the fee.
common_confusions: Training and self-certification are cumulative rather than alternatives: the self-certification attests that the training has been given.
A certification for one place of business does not cover another; each place of business at which the seller sells these products at retail needs its own.
The fee waiver for a DEA-registered pharmacy removes the $21 fee, not the duty to self-certify.
